views.title: The fleet
views.statement: Say which projects have a session alive, what each one is running, and how long since it did anything.
views.notes: What `proj` prints with no argument, and the screen every other command is reached from.

views.title: Sessions
views.statement: Show every Claude session on disk, newest first, and act on the one under the cursor.
views.notes: `proj sessions`. Driven by key: enter resumes, a adopts into a project, f forks at a chosen message, s stops, r removes. Piped or redirected it prints the same table without the cursor.

views.title: Doner
views.statement: Say whether the backstop that keeps a session working is on, whether its hook is installed, and which projects carry the tag.
views.notes: `proj doner`. The whole control surface is the doner tag; the Stop hook reads it live, so tagging a project is all there is to do.

views.title: Switch preview
views.statement: Show what moving a project to another coding tool would carry over, before anything is moved.
views.notes: `proj switch <project> <tool> --dry-run`. The same extraction the real switch performs, printed instead of written.

views.title: Model
views.statement: Set the model every new session starts with, and say which running sessions are still on the old one.
views.notes: `proj model <model>`. It writes Claude Code's own default rather than typing into panes, because driving /model past an autocomplete and a confirmation once left four sessions sitting on an unanswered picker.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: The base directory holds no projects. One dim line names the directory that was searched and the command that makes a project.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: The config file does not parse. One error line names the file, the line and what was expected, and the command exits non-zero.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: No Claude session exists on disk. One line says so; older sessions past the age cutoff are counted separately when there are any.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: The config cannot be read, so the list never opens and the error stands in its place.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: Nothing is tagged and the hook is not installed. Each line reports its own state and names the command that fixes it.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: The config cannot be read, so the tags cannot be looked up and the error is all there is.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: The project has no history to carry. It says nought turns and then prints the takeover prompt anyway, conversation section and all, empty.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: The target tool is not one proj knows. The error names the known tools and the config section that would add another.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: There is no project for the new default to apply to. The line says so and names the directory, instead of reading like a fleet-wide change.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: The config cannot be read, so the default is not written and nothing changes.

requirements.title: Say which sessions are alive
requirements.statement: A filled dot for a live session, a hollow one for a project without, a pin for one the daemon always recreates.

requirements.title: Say what each project runs
requirements.statement: The tool and the model a project is configured to run, so a project whose settings moved to a newer model does not keep showing the old one until it answers again.

requirements.title: Say how long since each project spoke
requirements.statement: One relative age per row, from the session when there is one and the directory when there is not, and older-than-the-cutoff projects folded into a count.

requirements.title: Say something when there is nothing
requirements.statement: An empty base directory says where proj looked and how a project is made, rather than printing nothing and exiting zero, which is indistinguishable from a broken install.

requirements.title: Show what each session was about
requirements.statement: Id, age, message count, project, the last thing asked and the last thing answered, so a session is recognised without opening it.

requirements.title: Act on the session under the cursor
requirements.statement: Resume it, adopt it into a project, fork it at a chosen message, stop it, or remove it, with the keys named on screen.

requirements.title: Stay usable without a terminal
requirements.statement: Piped or redirected, the same table prints without the cursor and without waiting for a key.

requirements.title: Say whether the backstop can act
requirements.statement: Whether doner is on, whether the Stop hook is installed in Claude Code's settings, and which projects carry the tag.

requirements.title: Say how to fix a missing hook
requirements.statement: "hook not installed" names `proj doner install`, the way the tag line names `proj tag add`, since the tag alone does nothing without the hook.

requirements.title: Say how much would survive the move
requirements.statement: How many turns were extracted and how many would reach the new tool, before anything is written or any session is touched.

requirements.title: Show the handoff as the new tool will read it
requirements.statement: The takeover prompt in full, so a bad translation is visible before it becomes someone's first message.

requirements.title: Say when there is nothing to carry
requirements.statement: A project with no history should stop at "nothing to carry" instead of printing a takeover prompt whose conversation section is empty.

requirements.title: Set the model new sessions start with
requirements.statement: One command writes Claude Code's own default, so every session started afterwards runs it, and no running session is typed into.

requirements.title: Name the sessions left behind
requirements.statement: A running session keeps the model it started with, so the command names the ones that differ and how to restart them. An alias ("opus") matches its own family, or every session in it would read as left behind the moment the family was set.

requirements.title: Say what was actually affected
requirements.statement: The line names what the change covers, so a fleet-wide change and a default written on a machine with no projects no longer read the same.

requirements.title: Fail on the config in one line
requirements.statement: Every command reads the same config, and when it does not parse each names the file, the line and what was expected, then exits non-zero without a usage dump.

stories.title: See the whole fleet at once
stories.statement: I keep a dozen projects going at the same time. I want one screen that says which have a session alive, what each is running and which have gone quiet, without opening any of them.

stories.title: Pick up yesterday's conversation
stories.statement: I want to find the session I was in yesterday by what it was about rather than by its id, and carry on from it, or branch it into a project of its own.

stories.title: Leave a session working
stories.statement: I want a session to keep going while I am away instead of stopping at the first natural pause, and I want to see at a glance which projects that is switched on for.

stories.title: Move a project to another tool
stories.statement: When one coding tool is going badly I want to move the project to another one and keep the conversation, and I want to see what would survive the move before it happens.

stories.title: Put the fleet on a new model
stories.statement: When a new model lands I want every project to start using it, and to be told which running sessions are still on the old one so I can restart those and no others.
